name: Bakbukiah
title: Levitical singer and temple servant
summary: Bakbukiah was a Levite who served as a singer and gatekeeper in the temple in Jerusalem after returning from the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the Levites responsible for praise and guarding the temple. His service was an important part of rebuilding religious worship in restored Israel.

keyEvents.title: Service among the Levites in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Bakbukiah is mentioned as one of the Levites who settled in Jerusalem after returning from exile. He was among those responsible for temple service.

keyEvents.title: Second to his brothers in praise
keyEvents.description: Bakbukiah served as second among his brothers in the Levitical praise service, together with Unni. He participated in the organized worship in the temple.

keyEvents.title: Gatekeeper service at the temples
keyEvents.description: Bakbukiah was among the Levites who served as gatekeepers at the storehouses by the gates and had responsibility for guarding the temple.

keyEvents.title: Service under Nehemiah's leadership
keyEvents.description: Under Nehemiah's rule and the rebuilding of Jerusalem, Bakbukiah played an important role in restoring the Levitical service in accordance with David's original arrangements.

keyEvents.title: Part of the genealogy of the Levites
keyEvents.description: Bakbukiah is recorded in the genealogies of the Levites who returned from Babylon, confirming his Levitical heritage and right to temple service.
